chunks: I said: 'The pigeons which are sent with a message from the remote places come back, while those sent from the nearby places do not come back.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When its feed is cut off, it will not come.'

key_terms.أُكُلُهُ: its feed/food — the regular provision given to a homing pigeon at its home base that motivates its return
key_terms.الْحَمَامُ: carrier pigeon — birds trained to carry messages between locations

ai.seo_question: Why do carrier pigeons released from far away return home but not from nearby places?
ai.summary: A questioner describes the paradox of carrier pigeons: those released from distant locations return home, while those released from nearby places do not. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a simple but profound explanation — when a pigeon's feed supply at home is cut off, it has no incentive to return. This hadith appears in a chapter on the use of pigeons as messenger birds, reflecting the Imam's practical knowledge of animal behavior and homing instincts, indicating that the bond formed through regular feeding is what draws the bird home.
